questionText:
Read the following excerpt on Nandalal Bose and the illumination of the Indian Constitution and answer the questions:

When the Constituent Assembly of India completed drafting the Constitution of the Republic of India, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru personally invited Nandalal Bose and his master students from Kala Bhavana, Santiniketan, to illustrate the original calligraphed manuscript. Working between 1949 and 1950, Nandalal executed 22 monumental header panels for the 22 parts of the Constitution, visually chronicling 5,000 years of Indian civilizational history. Painted in 1912 by master artist Nandalal Bose using watercolor and tempera on paper, 'Parthasarthi' (Charioteer of Partha) is a defining masterpiece of modern Indian mythological art. Set in the apocalyptic prelude to the Kurukshetra war from the Mahabharata, the painting portrays Lord Krishna acting as the divine charioteer for the Pandava warrior Arjuna. Krishna is depicted at the front of the war chariot, holding the reins of four spirited white horses with his left hand while raising and blowing the sacred conch shell Panchajanya with his right hand to declare the righteous battle. His celestial face radiates divine composure and majestic authority. Seated reverently behind Krishna in the chariot is warrior prince Arjuna, his mighty bow Gandiva resting beside him, gazing with complete faith and surrender at his divine charioteer. Nandalal uses sweeping calligraphic contours influenced by the Ajanta cave murals to create an atmosphere of heroic righteousness and cosmic destiny, conserved in the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi.
